newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX May natgas jumps to 5-week high with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX May natgas jumps to 5-week high with cash.

text.p: NYMEX spot Henry Hub natgas futures broke to a five-week high early Thursday in moderate activity, driven by reports of firmer physical prices and some follow-through technical buying to yesterday's strong close.
At 1150 EDT, May was up 6.5 cents at $2.07 per million British thermal units after climbing early to a new five-week high of $2.085. June jumped 7.4 cents to $2.12. Others were up.

"It's primarily technical triggered by (cool) weather. Technically, it looks constructive, and next week the Midwest and Northeast are going to stay below-normal which might be enough to keep the cash supported," said a Texas trader.

Chart traders said May's close Wednesday above $2 spooked the shorts and helped drive the spot month this morning above the channel line, another bullish technical indicator. They pegged key resistance at $2.095, the intraday high from March 10. May support points were still seen at $1.925, $1.88, $1.85 and $1.825.
June, which Wednesday broke a double top at $2.03 and rallied this morning to an 11-week high, seemed set to test next resistance at the $2.21-2.23 gap from mid-January.
But many remained skeptical current levels could be sustained, with storage well-above last year and more moderate spring weather bound to arrive soon.

"We've got (cool) weather now, but it can't continue for a whole lot longer. Until we see some A-C (air conditioning) load, which is at least a month away, my gut feel is that we'll drift back down," the trader said.
Temperatures in the Northeast and upper Midwest were expected to remain below normal into next week, but the South and Mid-Atlantic were forecast to moderate to more seasonal levels.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices jumped more than a nickel to the $2.05 area. Midcontinent pipes were up a similar amount to the low-$1.90s. Gas at the New York city gate also was quoted at least five cents higher in the low-$2.40s.
NYMEX said 26,772 Hub contracts traded at 1121 EDT. Hub open interest on April 16 rose 4,034 contracts to 183,444.
As of 1150 EDT, no NYMEX Permian or Alberta natgas futures were traded.

On KCBT, May rallied six cents to $1.95, while deferreds were steady to eight cents higher. The East/West spread widened by one-half cent to 12.0 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT open interest on April 16 rose 74 lots to 2,655.
